--- START OF SOURCE: adi.c ---
/**
 * This version is stamped on May 10, 2016
 *
 * Contact:
 *   Louis-Noel Pouchet <pouchet.ohio-state.edu>
 *   Tomofumi Yuki <tomofumi.yuki.fr>
 *
 * Web address: http://polybench.sourceforge.net
 */
/* adi.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "adi.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(u,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
      {
	u[i][j] =  (DATA_TYPE)(i + n-j) / n;
      }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
 
static 
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(u,N,N,n,n)) 

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("u");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf(POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, u[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("u");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
/* Based on a Fortran code fragment from Figure 5 of
 * "Automatic Data and Computation Decomposition on Distributed Memory Parallel Computers"
 * by Peizong Lee and Zvi Meir Kedem, TOPLAS, 2002
 */
static
void kernel_adi[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int tsteps, int n,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(u,N,N,n,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(v,N,N,n,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(p,N,N,n,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(q,N,N,n,n))
{
  int t, i, j;
  DATA_TYPE DX, DY, DT;
  DATA_TYPE B1, B2;
  DATA_TYPE mul1, mul2;
  DATA_TYPE a, b, c, d, e, f;

#pragma scop

  DX = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)/(DATA_TYPE)_PB_N;
  DY = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)/(DATA_TYPE)_PB_N;
  DT = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)/(DATA_TYPE)_PB_TSTEPS;
  B1 = SCALAR_VAL(2.0);
  B2 = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
  mul1 = B1 * DT / (DX * DX);
  mul2 = B2 * DT / (DY * DY);

  a = -mul1 /  SCALAR_VAL(2.0);
  b = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)+mul1;
  c = a;
  d = -mul2 / SCALAR_VAL(2.0);
  e = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)+mul2;
  f = d;

 for (t=1; t<=_PB_TSTEPS; t++) {
    //Column Sweep
    for (i=1; i<_PB_N-1; i++) {
      v[0][i] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
      p[i][0] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      q[i][0] = v[0][i];
      for (j=1; j<_PB_N-1; j++) {
        p[i][j] = -c / (a*p[i][j-1]+b);
        q[i][j] = (-d*u[j][i-1]+(SCALAR_VAL(1.0)+SCALAR_VAL(2.0)*d)*u[j][i] - f*u[j][i+1]-a*q[i][j-1])/(a*p[i][j-1]+b);
      }

      v[_PB_N-1][i] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
      for (j=_PB_N-2; j>=1; j--) {
        v[j][i] = p[i][j] * v[j+1][i] + q[i][j];
      }
    }
    //Row Sweep
    for (i=1; i<_PB_N-1; i++) {
      u[i][0] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
      p[i][0] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      q[i][0] = u[i][0];
      for (j=1; j<_PB_N-1; j++) {
        p[i][j] = -f / (d*p[i][j-1]+e);
        q[i][j] = (-a*v[i-1][j]+(SCALAR_VAL(1.0)+SCALAR_VAL(2.0)*a)*v[i][j] - c*v[i+1][j]-d*q[i][j-1])/(d*p[i][j-1]+e);
      }
      u[i][_PB_N-1] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
      for (j=_PB_N-2; j>=1; j--) {
        u[i][j] = p[i][j] * u[i][j+1] + q[i][j];
      }
    }
  }
#pragma endscop
}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int tsteps = TSTEPS;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(u, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(v, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(p, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(q, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_adi (tsteps, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(v), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(p), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(q));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(u);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(v);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(p);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(q);

  return 0;
}

--- END OF SOURCE: adi.c ---

--- START OF MODEL: adi-01 ---
domain:
    # Global index space
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)              # time steps
    i: dim in [0, N)                   # spatial index in x-direction
    j: dim in [0, N)                   # spatial index in y-direction

data:
    # All 2D arrays are logically N×N and stored row-major as in C: a[i][j] -> base + (i * N + j)
    u[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
        # solution array; only u is observed outside the kernel

    v[i, j]: scratch DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
        # intermediate array; used only within kernel_adi

    p[i, j]: scratch DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
        # tridiagonal forward coefficients (scratch, overwritten every sweep)

    q[i, j]: scratch DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
        # tridiagonal RHS / modified RHS (scratch, overwritten every sweep)

    # Scalar coefficients computed once per kernel invocation
    DX: scalar DATA_TYPE
    DY: scalar DATA_TYPE
    DT: scalar DATA_TYPE
    B1: scalar DATA_TYPE
    B2: scalar DATA_TYPE
    mul1: scalar DATA_TYPE
    mul2: scalar DATA_TYPE
    a: scalar DATA_TYPE
    b: scalar DATA_TYPE
    c: scalar DATA_TYPE
    d: scalar DATA_TYPE
    e: scalar DATA_TYPE
    f: scalar DATA_TYPE
    center_col: scalar DATA_TYPE     # 1 + 2*d
    center_row: scalar DATA_TYPE     # 1 + 2*a

parameters:
    N:       int                     # grid size, matches C macro N
    TSTEPS:  int                     # number of time steps, matches C macro TSTEPS

computation:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Precompute coefficients exactly as in the C code (same FP semantics)
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    DX = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) / (DATA_TYPE) N
    DY = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) / (DATA_TYPE) N
    DT = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) / (DATA_TYPE) TSTEPS
    B1 = SCALAR_VAL(2.0)
    B2 = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)
    mul1 = B1 * DT / (DX * DX)
    mul2 = B2 * DT / (DY * DY)

    a = -mul1 / SCALAR_VAL(2.0)
    b = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) + mul1
    c = a
    d = -mul2 / SCALAR_VAL(2.0)
    e = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) + mul2
    f = d

    # hoisted common subexpressions from the inner loops
    center_col = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) + SCALAR_VAL(2.0) * d   # 1 + 2*d
    center_row = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) + SCALAR_VAL(2.0) * a   # 1 + 2*a

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Time stepping loop (must remain sequential)
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):
        #========================
        # Column sweep
        #========================
        # For each interior "column index" i, solve a tridiagonal system
        # along j (0..N-1). Dependency is along j only, so columns (different i)
        # are independent and can be processed in parallel.
        for i in seq([1, N-1)):
            # Boundary conditions and initialization for this 1D system
            v[0, i] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)
            p[i, 0] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0)
            q[i, 0] = v[0, i]              # = 1.0

            # Forward recursion in j: compute p[i, j], q[i, j]
            COL_FWD:
            for j in seq([1, N-1)):
                # Common denominator used by both p and q updates
                den_col = a * p[i, j-1] + b

                p[i, j] = -c / den_col

                # Numerator for q update; reuses precomputed center_col = 1 + 2*d
                num_col = -d * u[j,   i-1] \
                          + center_col * u[j, i] \
                          - f * u[j,   i+1] \
                          - a * q[i,  j-1]

                q[i, j] = num_col / den_col

            # Backward substitution using p and q, along j decreasing
            v[N-1, i] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)

            COL_BWD:
            # Conceptually: for j = N-2 down to 1 (strictly decreasing).
            # We denote this with a dedicated "reverse" sequential iterator.
            for j in seq_reverse([1, N-1)):    # j: N-2, N-3, ..., 1
                v[j, i] = p[i, j] * v[j+1, i] + q[i, j]

        #========================
        # Row sweep
        #========================
        # For each interior "row index" i, solve a tridiagonal system
        # along j (0..N-1) using v as input and writing u.
        # Again, dependency is along j only, so rows (different i)
        # are independent.
        for i in seq([1, N-1)):
            # Boundary conditions and initialization for this 1D system
            u[i, 0] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)
            p[i, 0] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0)
            q[i, 0] = u[i, 0]               # = 1.0

            # Forward recursion in j: compute p[i, j], q[i, j]
            ROW_FWD:
            for j in seq([1, N-1)):
                # Common denominator used by both p and q updates
                den_row = d * p[i, j-1] + e

                p[i, j] = -f / den_row

                # Numerator for q update; reuses precomputed center_row = 1 + 2*a
                num_row = -a * v[i-1, j] \
                          + center_row * v[i, j] \
                          - c * v[i+1, j] \
                          - d * q[i,  j-1]

                q[i, j] = num_row / den_row

            # Backward substitution using p and q, along j decreasing
            u[i, N-1] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)

            ROW_BWD:
            # Conceptually: for j = N-2 down to 1 (strictly decreasing).
            for j in seq_reverse([1, N-1)):    # j: N-2, N-3, ..., 1
                u[i, j] = p[i, j] * u[i, j+1] + q[i, j]

dependencies:
    # Forward column sweep: recurrences along j within each (t, i)
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        p(t, i, j-1) -> p(t, i, j)
        q(t, i, j-1) -> q(t, i, j)

    # Backward column sweep: recurrences along j within each (t, i)
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        v(t, j+1, i) -> v(t, j, i)

    # Forward row sweep: recurrences along j within each (t, i)
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        p(t, i, j-1) -> p(t, i, j)
        q(t, i, j-1) -> q(t, i, j)

    # Backward row sweep: recurrences along j within each (t, i)
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        u(t, i, j+1) -> u(t, i, j)

    # Time stepping: step t+1 depends on completed step t via u
    for t in [0, TSTEPS-1]:
        { all writes to u at time t } -> { all reads/writes to u at time t+1 }

optimization:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Parallelize across independent tridiagonal solves
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # For a fixed time t, each column (in the column sweep) and each row
    # (in the row sweep) is an independent 1D tridiagonal solve: there are
    # no data dependencies across different i values, only along j.
    #
    # This exposes abundant coarse-grain parallelism, ideal for the
    # 32-core (64-thread) x64 target machine.

    parallelize(i)
        # Apply to both the column-sweep and row-sweep i-loops inside the time loop.
        # Can map to OpenMP "parallel for" with static scheduling.
        # Each thread only touches disjoint rows of p, q, u, v -> no races.

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Cache-friendly blocking in the spatial dimension
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile the i-dimension so that each thread works on a contiguous block of
    # rows/columns that fits in cache, improving reuse of p, q, u, v lines and
    # reducing TLB pressure.

    block(i, ii, TI_col)
        # Column sweep: split i into outer tile index ii and inner index i within tile.
        # Example: TI_col ≈ 64 or 128 (tunable based on LLC size).

    block(i, ii, TI_row)
        # Row sweep: similarly tile i for the row sweep; TI_row can be tuned separately.

    hoist(ii)
        # Execute tiles (ii) at the outermost level inside each time step,
        # with inner loops over i, j as in the computation. This keeps each
        # tile's working set resident in cache as much as possible.

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Respect recurrences but unroll for ILP
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # The j-loops contain true recurrences (tridiagonal forward/backward passes),
    # so they must remain sequential in j, but can still benefit from modest
    # unrolling to improve instruction-level parallelism and hide latency.

    unroll(j, 4) in COL_FWD
    unroll(j, 4) in COL_BWD
    unroll(j, 4) in ROW_FWD
    unroll(j, 4) in ROW_BWD
        # Unroll factor 4 is a reasonable default; it can be tuned.
        # Unrolling preserves the dependency order along j but exposes more
        # operations for the out-of-order core to schedule.

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Vectorization where dependencies allow
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Due to j-recursions, the main j-loops are not straightforwardly vectorizable
    # across j. However, we can:
    #
    #  - Vectorize simple boundary initialization loops over i.
    #  - Vectorize within each i-tile over i when operating on independent
    #    rows/columns, e.g., boundary writes or other point-wise operations.

    vectorize(i, SIMD_WIDTH)
        # Apply to boundary loops:
        #   v[0, i] = 1, v[N-1, i] = 1, u[i, 0] = 1, u[i, N-1] = 1
        # SIMD_WIDTH depends on DATA_TYPE (e.g., 4 or 8 for double/float AVX).

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Arithmetic CSE and strength reduction inside hot loops
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # These are already reflected in the 'computation' section but summarized here.
    #
    #  - Precompute center_col = 1 + 2*d and center_row = 1 + 2*a once.
    #  - In each (i, j) iteration of the forward passes, compute the shared
    #    denominator (den_col or den_row) only once, then reuse it for both p
    #    and q updates. This removes one multiplication and one addition per
    #    iteration compared to the naive formulation.
    #
    #  - Keep DX, DY, DT, mul1, mul2, a..f as loop-invariant scalars, as modeled,
    #    so that the compiler does not redundantly recompute them in the inner loops.

    hoist(center_col)
    hoist(center_row)
        # Explicitly mark these as hoisted scalars used in inner loops.

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Memory usage and temporaries
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # No additional large data structures are introduced beyond u, v, p, q.
    # All extra quantities (den_col, num_col, den_row, num_row) are scalars
    # local to the inner loops and do not increase the asymptotic memory
    # footprint. Total memory stays within the original 4*N^2 DATA_TYPE
    # elements plus a negligible number of scalars (< 50% overhead constraint).
--- END OF MODEL: adi-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: adi-02 ---
domain:
    # Time and 2D space.
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)       # time steps
    i: dim in [0, N)            # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)            # column index

data:
    # Solution grids, stored row-major as in the original C code.
    u[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j     # u[i][j]
    v[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j     # v[i][j]

    # Tridiagonal-solver temporaries:
    # In the optimized version we store p and q column-major (j-major),
    # i.e., transposed relative to u and v. This matches the optimized
    # loop order (j outer, i inner) and makes inner-loop access to p,q
    # contiguous and vectorizable.
    p[i, j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> j * N + i      # column-major
    q[i, j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> j * N + i      # column-major

parameters:
    # Problem sizes.
    N: int                # grid size
    T: int = TSTEPS       # number of time steps

    # Scalar coefficients, computed once per kernel call (hoisted out of t).
    DX: DATA_TYPE = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE)N
    DY: DATA_TYPE = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE)N
    DT: DATA_TYPE = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE)T

    B1: DATA_TYPE = 2.0
    B2: DATA_TYPE = 1.0

    mul1: DATA_TYPE = B1 * DT / (DX * DX)
    mul2: DATA_TYPE = B2 * DT / (DY * DY)

    a: DATA_TYPE = -mul1 / 2.0
    b: DATA_TYPE = 1.0 + mul1
    c: DATA_TYPE = a
    d: DATA_TYPE = -mul2 / 2.0
    e: DATA_TYPE = 1.0 + mul2
    f: DATA_TYPE = d

    # Precompute the “center” stencil coefficients (originally 1 + 2*d and 1 + 2*a).
    center_col: DATA_TYPE = 1.0 + 2.0 * d   # used in column sweep
    center_row: DATA_TYPE = 1.0 + 2.0 * a   # used in row sweep

computation:
    # The time loop is strictly sequential: step t+1 cannot start before step t finishes.
    for t in seq([0, T)):

        # === Column sweep (implicit in j, one independent tridiagonal system per i) ===
        # We operate on interior indices i, j in [1, N-1), i.e., 1..N-2.
        # Boundary points j = 0 and j = N-1 are set explicitly.

        # 1) Column boundary conditions and initial values for the forward sweep.
        COL_BC_TOP:
            for i in [1, N-1):
                v[0,    i] = 1.0          # top boundary for v
                p[i, 0]  = 0.0           # p(i, j=0)
                q[i, 0]  = 1.0           # q(i, j=0) = v(0, i) = 1

        # 2) Forward sweep along j (Thomas factorization).
        #    j is sequential due to recurrences, i is independent.
        COL_FWD:
            for j in seq([1, N-1)):      # j = 1..N-2
                for i in [1, N-1):       # i = 1..N-2
                    denom_col = a * p[i, j-1] + b
                    p[i, j] = -c / denom_col
                    q[i, j] = (-d * u[j, i-1]
                               + center_col * u[j, i]
                               - f * u[j, i+1]
                               - a * q[i, j-1]) / denom_col

        # 3) Column boundary condition at j = N-1 for backward substitution.
        COL_BC_BOTTOM:
            for i in [1, N-1):
                v[N-1, i] = 1.0          # bottom boundary for v

        # 4) Backward sweep along j (Thomas back substitution).
        #    Mathematically: v[j, i] = p[i, j] * v[j+1, i] + q[i, j],
        #    for j = N-2, ..., 1.
        COL_BWD:
            for j in seq([1, N-1)):      # scheduled in decreasing j due to deps
                for i in [1, N-1):
                    v[j, i] = p[i, j] * v[j+1, i] + q[i, j]

        # At this point v holds the intermediate solution after the column sweep.

        # === Row sweep (implicit in i, one independent tridiagonal system per i) ===
        # Same structure but now operating on u using v as input.

        # 5) Row boundary conditions and initial values for the forward sweep.
        ROW_BC_LEFT:
            for i in [1, N-1):
                u[i, 0] = 1.0            # left boundary for u
                p[i, 0] = 0.0            # reuse p,q as scratch
                q[i, 0] = 1.0            # q(i, j=0) = u(i,0) = 1

        # 6) Forward sweep along j (Thomas factorization for each row).
        ROW_FWD:
            for j in seq([1, N-1)):      # j = 1..N-2
                for i in [1, N-1):
                    denom_row = d * p[i, j-1] + e
                    p[i, j] = -f / denom_row
                    q[i, j] = (-a * v[i-1, j]
                               + center_row * v[i, j]
                               - c * v[i+1, j]
                               - d * q[i, j-1]) / denom_row

        # 7) Row boundary condition at j = N-1 for backward substitution.
        ROW_BC_RIGHT:
            for i in [1, N-1):
                u[i, N-1] = 1.0          # right boundary for u

        # 8) Backward sweep along j.
        #    Mathematically: u[i, j] = p[i, j] * u[i, j+1] + q[i, j],
        #    for j = N-2, ..., 1.
        ROW_BWD:
            for j in seq([1, N-1)):      # scheduled in decreasing j due to deps
                for i in [1, N-1):
                    u[i, j] = p[i, j] * u[i, j+1] + q[i, j]

dependencies:
    # Dependencies within a fixed time step t.

    # Column forward sweep recurrences along j:
    # p[i, j] and q[i, j] depend on p[i, j-1], q[i, j-1].
    for t in [0, T), i in [1, N-1), j in [2, N-1):
        COL_FWD(t, i, j-1) -> COL_FWD(t, i, j)

    # Column backward sweep recurrences along j:
    # v[j, i] depends on v[j+1, i].
    for t in [0, T), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-2):
        COL_BWD(t, i, j+1) -> COL_BWD(t, i, j)

    # Row forward sweep recurrences along j:
    for t in [0, T), i in [1, N-1), j in [2, N-1):
        ROW_FWD(t, i, j-1) -> ROW_FWD(t, i, j)

    # Row backward sweep recurrences along j:
    for t in [0, T), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-2):
        ROW_BWD(t, i, j+1) -> ROW_BWD(t, i, j)

    # Phase ordering within a time step is given by the nesting/order in 'computation':
    # COL_BC_TOP -> COL_FWD -> COL_BC_BOTTOM -> COL_BWD
    # then ROW_BC_LEFT -> ROW_FWD -> ROW_BC_RIGHT -> ROW_BWD.
    # The outer for t in seq(...) enforces that *all* work at time t
    # finishes before any work at time t+1 starts.

optimization:
    # 1) Tile the i-dimension to improve cache locality and to provide
    #    coarse-grain work units for parallel threads.
    #    IB is a tunable tile size (e.g., 64 or 128, based on L1/L2 sizes).
    block(i, I, IB)

    # 2) Parallelize over the outer i-tiles (dimension I).
    #    Each tridiagonal system along j is independent for each i, so we
    #    can safely run different i-tiles in parallel in both sweeps.
    parallelize(I)

    # 3) Vectorize the innermost i-dimension inside each tile for the
    #    compute-intensive sweeps. The j-dimension remains scalar because
    #    of the Thomas recurrences.
    #    FACTOR can be set to match the SIMD width (e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles).
    vectorize(i, FACTOR)

    # 4) The change of layout for p and q (declared above) is itself an
    #    optimization: it makes p[i, j] and q[i, j] contiguous in memory
    #    when iterating with j outer / i inner, enabling efficient SIMD
    #    loads/stores and reducing cache misses without increasing memory
    #    footprint.

    # 5) Scalar parameters (DX, DY, DT, B1, B2, mul1, mul2, a..f,
    #    center_col, center_row) are already hoisted out of the time loop
    #    in this model; no further hoisting is needed.
--- END OF MODEL: adi-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: adi-03 ---
domain:
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)          # time step index; corresponds to C loop t = 1..TSTEPS
    i: dim in [0, N)               # spatial index in x-direction
    j: dim in [0, N)               # spatial index in y-direction

data:
    # 2D solution arrays, row-major: element (i,j) at linear index i * N + j
    u[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
    v[i, j]: temp  DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Tridiagonal solver coefficients (per line i, along coordinate j)
    p[i, j]: temp  DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
    q[i, j]: temp  DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

parameters:
    # Grid and time sizes
    N:       int       # problem size (both dimensions)
    TSTEPS:  int       # number of time steps

    # Physical / numerical constants
    B1: DATA_TYPE = 2.0
    B2: DATA_TYPE = 1.0

    # Derived scalars (do not depend on t, i, or j)
    DX:  DATA_TYPE = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE) N
    DY:  DATA_TYPE = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE) N
    DT:  DATA_TYPE = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE) TSTEPS

    mul1: DATA_TYPE = B1 * DT / (DX * DX)
    mul2: DATA_TYPE = B2 * DT / (DY * DY)

    a: DATA_TYPE = -mul1 / 2.0
    b: DATA_TYPE =  1.0 + mul1
    c: DATA_TYPE =  a
    d: DATA_TYPE = -mul2 / 2.0
    e: DATA_TYPE =  1.0 + mul2
    f: DATA_TYPE =  d

    # Optional tuning parameters (used only in optimization directives)
    TI: int  # tile size for the i-dimension, 1 <= TI <= N
    VF: int  # vector width (elements) for SIMD along i

computation:
    # Time stepping loop
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):
        #-----------------
        # Column sweep: solve along j for each fixed i, writing v from u
        #-----------------
        for i in [1, N-1):
            COL_TOP_AND_INIT:
                u_top = 1.0           # Dirichlet boundary value
                v[0, i] = u_top
                p[i, 0] = 0.0
                q[i, 0] = v[0, i]     # = 1.0

            COL_FORWARD:
                for j in seq([1, N-1)):
                    # p and q forward recurrence (Thomas algorithm)
                    p[i, j] = -c / (a * p[i, j-1] + b)
                    q[i, j] = (
                        -d * u[j, i-1] +
                        (1.0 + 2.0 * d) * u[j, i] -
                        f * u[j, i+1] -
                        a * q[i, j-1]
                    ) / (a * p[i, j-1] + b)

            COL_BOTTOM:
                v[N-1, i] = u_top    # bottom Dirichlet boundary = 1.0

            COL_BACKWARD:
                # j descends: j = N-2, N-3, ..., 1
                for j in seq([1, N-1)) descending:
                    # backward substitution for v along j
                    v[j, i] = p[i, j] * v[j+1, i] + q[i, j]

        #-----------------
        # Row sweep: solve along j for each fixed i, writing u from v
        #-----------------
        for i in [1, N-1):
            ROW_LEFT_AND_INIT:
                u_left = 1.0          # Dirichlet boundary value
                u[i, 0] = u_left
                p[i, 0] = 0.0
                q[i, 0] = u[i, 0]     # = 1.0

            ROW_FORWARD:
                for j in seq([1, N-1)):
                    # p and q forward recurrence (Thomas algorithm)
                    p[i, j] = -f / (d * p[i, j-1] + e)
                    q[i, j] = (
                        -a * v[i-1, j] +
                        (1.0 + 2.0 * a) * v[i, j] -
                        c * v[i+1, j] -
                        d * q[i, j-1]
                    ) / (d * p[i, j-1] + e)

            ROW_RIGHT:
                u[i, N-1] = u_left    # right Dirichlet boundary = 1.0

            ROW_BACKWARD:
                # j descends: j = N-2, N-3, ..., 1
                for j in seq([1, N-1)) descending:
                    # backward substitution for u along j
                    u[i, j] = p[i, j] * u[i, j+1] + q[i, j]

dependencies:
    # Time stepping: each time step depends on the result of the previous one.
    for t in [0, TSTEPS-1):
        # Entire step t must complete before step t+1 starts.
        ROW_BACKWARD(t, i, j) for all i, j -> COL_TOP_AND_INIT(t+1, i) for all i

    # Within a given time step t:

    # Column sweep per line i:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1):
        # Initialization before forward sweep
        COL_TOP_AND_INIT(t, i) -> COL_FORWARD(t, i, 1)

        # Forward recurrence along j (j increases)
        for j in [2, N-1):
            COL_FORWARD(t, i, j-1) -> COL_FORWARD(t, i, j)

        # Bottom boundary set after forward sweep
        COL_FORWARD(t, i, N-2) -> COL_BOTTOM(t, i)

        # Backward substitution along j (j decreases)
        COL_BOTTOM(t, i) -> COL_BACKWARD(t, i, N-2)
        for j in [1, N-2):
            COL_BACKWARD(t, i, j+1) -> COL_BACKWARD(t, i, j)

    # Row sweep per line i:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1):
        # Row sweep for a given t starts only after the entire column sweep has finished,
        # because it reads v computed in the column sweep.
        for j in [1, N-1):
            COL_BACKWARD(t, k, j) for all k in [1, N-1) -> ROW_LEFT_AND_INIT(t, i)

        ROW_LEFT_AND_INIT(t, i) -> ROW_FORWARD(t, i, 1)

        # Forward recurrence along j (j increases)
        for j in [2, N-1):
            ROW_FORWARD(t, i, j-1) -> ROW_FORWARD(t, i, j)

        # Right boundary set after forward sweep
        ROW_FORWARD(t, i, N-2) -> ROW_RIGHT(t, i)

        # Backward substitution along j (j decreases)
        ROW_RIGHT(t, i) -> ROW_BACKWARD(t, i, N-2)
        for j in [1, N-2):
            ROW_BACKWARD(t, i, j+1) -> ROW_BACKWARD(t, i, j)

optimization:
    #-----------------
    # Scalar and invariant-hoisting optimizations
    #-----------------
    # All coefficients (DX, DY, DT, mul1, mul2, a, b, c, d, e, f) and the
    # Dirichlet boundary value 1.0 are invariant across t, i, j.
    # Hoist their computation outside the t-loop in generated code.
    hoist(t)

    # Within each forward recurrence, the denominator (a * p[i,j-1] + b) or
    # (d * p[i,j-1] + e) is common to the two updates of p and q.
    # A code generator should introduce a loop-private temporary for this
    # denominator to avoid recomputing the multiply-add:
    #   den_c = a * p[i,j-1] + b
    #   p[i,j] = -c / den_c
    #   q[i,j] = (...) / den_c
    # (This reduces work while preserving IEEE-754 semantics, because the
    # multiply-add is evaluated once instead of twice but with identical operands.)

    #-----------------
    # Parallelism across independent 1D lines
    #-----------------
    # For each time step and each sweep, lines indexed by i are independent:
    # the recurrences are only along j. We can therefore parallelize
    # the outer i-dimension.
    parallelize(i) in {
        COL_TOP_AND_INIT, COL_FORWARD, COL_BOTTOM, COL_BACKWARD,
        ROW_LEFT_AND_INIT, ROW_FORWARD, ROW_RIGHT, ROW_BACKWARD
    }

    # To improve cache reuse and load balancing on 32 cores, tile the i-dimension
    # and parallelize over tiles. TI is a tunable tile size (e.g., 32..256).
    block(i, Ii, TI)
    parallelize(Ii)

    #-----------------
    # Instruction-level parallelism and SIMD
    #-----------------
    # j-loops implement a Thomas algorithm and must remain sequential
    # in j to respect the p/q and u/v recurrences. However, within each
    # line i we can expose ILP by modest unrolling of the j loops.
    unroll(j, 4) in {COL_FORWARD, COL_BACKWARD, ROW_FORWARD, ROW_BACKWARD}

    # There are no true dependences along i for fixed (t, j), so within a tile we
    # can vectorize across i. This effectively computes several independent
    # tridiagonal systems in lock-step.
    # A code generator can realize this by strip-mining i inside each tile and
    # mapping the inner i-loop to SIMD lanes.
    vectorize(i, VF) in {
        COL_FORWARD, COL_BACKWARD,
        ROW_FORWARD, ROW_BACKWARD
    }

    #-----------------
    # Memory hierarchy considerations
    #-----------------
    # - Keep u, v, p, q in row-major layout as in the original code.
    # - The i-tiling ensures that each thread repeatedly works on a subset of
    #   rows/columns, improving L1/L2 locality for u, v, p, and q.
    # - No additional large buffers are introduced; extra storage is limited
    #   to a few per-thread scalars (e.g., denominators), well below the
    #   allowed +50% memory overhead.
--- END OF MODEL: adi-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: adi-04 ---
domain:
    # Time dimension
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)

    # 2D spatial grid
    i: dim in [0, N)        # first index in C code
    j: dim in [0, N)        # second index in C code

data:
    # Main solution fields, row-major
    u[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # u[i][j]
    v[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # v[i][j]

    # Tridiagonal solver temporaries, row-major
    p[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # p[i][j], reused each sweep
    q[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # q[i][j], reused each sweep

    # Scalar coefficients (loop-invariant w.r.t. t, i, j)
    DX: scalar DATA_TYPE
    DY: scalar DATA_TYPE
    DT: scalar DATA_TYPE
    B1: scalar DATA_TYPE
    B2: scalar DATA_TYPE
    mul1: scalar DATA_TYPE
    mul2: scalar DATA_TYPE
    a: scalar DATA_TYPE
    b: scalar DATA_TYPE
    c: scalar DATA_TYPE
    d: scalar DATA_TYPE
    e: scalar DATA_TYPE
    f: scalar DATA_TYPE

    # Extra precomputed constants to eliminate repeated arithmetic
    gd: scalar DATA_TYPE      # = 1 + 2*d
    ga: scalar DATA_TYPE      # = 1 + 2*a

parameters:
    N:       int              # spatial grid size
    TSTEPS:  int              # number of time steps

computation:
    # Coefficient setup (once, outside time loop; identical to C code algebraically)
    DX = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE) N
    DY = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE) N
    DT = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE) TSTEPS

    B1 = 2.0
    B2 = 1.0

    mul1 = B1 * DT / (DX * DX)
    mul2 = B2 * DT / (DY * DY)

    a = -mul1 / 2.0
    b = 1.0 + mul1
    c = a
    d = -mul2 / 2.0
    e = 1.0 + mul2
    f = d

    # Precompute constants that are invariant across all loops
    gd = 1.0 + 2.0 * d       # used in column sweep q-update
    ga = 1.0 + 2.0 * a       # used in row sweep q-update

    # Time stepping: fully sequential in t
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):

        # ============================================================
        # 1) COLUMN SWEEP: solve tridiagonal systems along "columns"
        #    (fix second index i, sweep over j)
        # ============================================================

        # 1a) Initialize boundary conditions and forward-sweep seeds
        #     v(0, i) = 1, p(i, 0) = 0, q(i, 0) = v(0, i) = 1
        for i in [1, N-1):
            v[0, i] = 1.0
            p[i, 0] = 0.0
            q[i, 0] = v[0, i]   # = 1.0

        # 1b) Forward sweep for p and q along j (Thomas algorithm)
        #     Recurrence is along j, i-lines are independent.
        for j in seq([1, N-1)):
            for i in [1, N-1):
                denom1 = a * p[i, j-1] + b        # common subexpression

                p[i, j] = -c / denom1

                q[i, j] =
                    ( -d * u[j, i-1]
                      + gd * u[j, i]
                      - f * u[j, i+1]
                      - a * q[i, j-1] ) / denom1

        # 1c) Set opposite boundary for v
        for i in [1, N-1):
            v[N-1, i] = 1.0

        # 1d) Backward sweep in j to update v using p and q
        #     v(j, i) depends on v(j+1, i), so j must run in descending order.
        for j in seq([1, N-1)) descending:
            for i in [1, N-1):
                v[j, i] = p[i, j] * v[j+1, i] + q[i, j]

        # ============================================================
        # 2) ROW SWEEP: solve tridiagonal systems along "rows"
        #    (fix first index i, sweep over j)
        # ============================================================

        # 2a) Initialize boundary conditions and forward-sweep seeds
        #     u(i, 0) = 1, p(i, 0) = 0, q(i, 0) = u(i, 0) = 1
        for i in [1, N-1):
            u[i, 0] = 1.0
            p[i, 0] = 0.0
            q[i, 0] = u[i, 0]   # = 1.0

        # 2b) Forward sweep for p and q along j using v
        for j in seq([1, N-1)):
            for i in [1, N-1):
                denom2 = d * p[i, j-1] + e        # common subexpression

                p[i, j] = -f / denom2

                q[i, j] =
                    ( -a * v[i-1, j]
                      + ga * v[i, j]
                      - c * v[i+1, j]
                      - d * q[i, j-1] ) / denom2

        # 2c) Set opposite boundary for u
        for i in [1, N-1):
            u[i, N-1] = 1.0

        # 2d) Backward sweep in j to update u using p and q
        for j in seq([1, N-1)) descending:
            for i in [1, N-1):
                u[i, j] = p[i, j] * u[i, j+1] + q[i, j]

dependencies:
    # Time dimension: each time step depends on the previous one
    for t in [0, TSTEPS-1):
        kernel(t) -> kernel(t+1)

    # Within a single time step t, recurrences along j (per (sweep, i)):
    # Column sweep forward:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        (p_fwd(t, i, j-1) -> p_fwd(t, i, j))
        (q_fwd_col(t, i, j-1) -> q_fwd_col(t, i, j))

    # Column sweep backward:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        (v_bwd(t, i, j+1) -> v_bwd(t, i, j))

    # Row sweep forward:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        (p_fwd_row(t, i, j-1) -> p_fwd_row(t, i, j))
        (q_fwd_row(t, i, j-1) -> q_fwd_row(t, i, j))

    # Row sweep backward:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        (u_bwd(t, i, j+1) -> u_bwd(t, i, j))

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Hoist loop-invariant scalar computations
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # DX, DY, DT, B1, B2, mul1, mul2, a, b, c, d, e, f, gd, ga
    # do not depend on t, i, or j. Compute them once before the
    # time loop and treat them as constants during the kernel.
    #
    # This removes repeated divisions and multiplications inside
    # the hotspot loops.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # scalar_hoist: precompute scalar expressions outside loop dim
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    scalar_hoist({DX, DY, DT,
                  B1, B2,
                  mul1, mul2,
                  a, b, c, d, e, f,
                  gd, ga}, t)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Exploit parallelism in the spatial dimension
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # For fixed (t, j), all i-iterations of the forward/backward
    # sweeps are independent (dependencies are only along j).
    #
    # We therefore parallelize across i, using tiling to control
    # cache working-set size and to balance load across cores.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # TI: tunable tile size for i (e.g., 128 or 256 to fit L1/L2)
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    block(i, I, TI)          # tile i into outer tile-dim I and inner dim i
    parallelize(I)           # run tiles in parallel (e.g., via OpenMP)

    # Apply this tiling and parallelization consistently to all
    # i-nested loops in both column and row sweeps:
    #  - Column forward (j outer, I tile, i inner)
    #  - Column backward (j outer, I tile, i inner)
    #  - Row forward (j outer, I tile, i inner)
    #  - Row backward (j outer, I tile, i inner)
    #
    # Boundary-only loops over i (1a, 1c, 2a, 2c) can also be
    # parallelized over I without correctness issues.

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Enable SIMD vectorization along i
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # After restructuring the sweeps to have j sequential and i
    # independent, we can vectorize along i. All accesses in the
    # inner loops are to contiguous memory in the second index:
    #  - u[j, i-1..i+1], v[j±1, i], p[i, j], q[i, j]
    #
    # VW should match the hardware SIMD width for DATA_TYPE
    # (e.g., 4 for AVX2 double, 8 for AVX-512 float).
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    vectorize(i, VW)

    # Optionally unroll the j loops to improve ILP in the presence
    # of recurrences, without changing dependencies:
    unroll(j, 2)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Loop interchange and phase reorganization
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Compared to the original C:
    #  - The forward and backward sweeps were originally nested
    #    as: for i { for j { ... } }, with j as inner loop.
    #  - We have logically reorganized each sweep into four phases:
    #      (init in i), (forward in j), (boundary in i),
    #      (backward in j),
    #    and within the forward/backward phases, we interchange
    #    loops so that j is the sequential outer loop and i is the
    #    inner (vectorizable/parallel) loop.
    #
    # This preserves the j-recursions but exposes much better
    # spatial locality (contiguous access in i) and parallelism.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    interchange(i, j)  # applied to the inner sweeps as described above

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Arithmetic-strength reduction / common-subexpression reuse
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # For each (t, i, j) in the forward sweeps we reuse:
    #  - denom1 = a * p[i, j-1] + b
    #  - denom2 = d * p[i, j-1] + e
    # across p and q updates, avoiding recomputing the denominator.
    #
    # We also precompute:
    #  - gd = 1 + 2*d
    #  - ga = 1 + 2*a
    #
    # so that the inner loops use only multiplications and additions
    # with precomputed scalars, minimizing expensive divisions and
    # repeated additions with constants.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # cse: treat recurring denominators as explicit temporaries
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    cse({a * p[i, j-1] + b,
         d * p[i, j-1] + e},
        scope = {column_forward, row_forward})

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Memory considerations
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # No extra large data structures are introduced beyond the
    # original u, v, p, q. Scalar temporaries and denominators are
    # kept in registers or the stack. The memory footprint therefore
    # stays within the original footprint (well below +50%).
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
--- END OF MODEL: adi-04 ---

--- START OF MODEL: adi-05 ---
domain:
    # Time and spatial dimensions.
    t:  dim in [0, TSTEPS)        # time steps
    i:  dim in [0, N)             # x-direction index
    j:  dim in [0, N)             # y-direction index
    jb: dim in [1, N-1)           # helper for backward sweeps; physical index is (N-1-jb)

data:
    # Main solution array, updated in-place every time step.
    u[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # row-major

    # Temporary arrays reused at each time step.
    v[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # intermediate solution, row-major
    p[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # tridiagonal coefficient
    q[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # tridiagonal RHS accumulator

    # Scalar coefficients (computed once, then reused).
    DX:         scalar DATA_TYPE
    DY:         scalar DATA_TYPE
    DT:         scalar DATA_TYPE
    B1:         scalar DATA_TYPE
    B2:         scalar DATA_TYPE
    mul1:       scalar DATA_TYPE
    mul2:       scalar DATA_TYPE
    a:          scalar DATA_TYPE
    b:          scalar DATA_TYPE
    c:          scalar DATA_TYPE
    d:          scalar DATA_TYPE
    e:          scalar DATA_TYPE
    f:          scalar DATA_TYPE
    alpha_col:  scalar DATA_TYPE   # = 1 + 2*d
    alpha_row:  scalar DATA_TYPE   # = 1 + 2*a

parameters:
    N:      int
    TSTEPS: int

computation:
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Coefficient initialization (loop-invariant w.r.t. t)
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    INIT_CONST:
        DX        = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) / (DATA_TYPE)N
        DY        = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) / (DATA_TYPE)N
        DT        = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) / (DATA_TYPE)TSTEPS
        B1        = SCALAR_VAL(2.0)
        B2        = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)
        mul1      = B1 * DT / (DX * DX)
        mul2      = B2 * DT / (DY * DY)
        a         = -mul1 / SCALAR_VAL(2.0)
        b         = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) + mul1
        c         = a
        d         = -mul2 / SCALAR_VAL(2.0)
        e         = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) + mul2
        f         = d
        alpha_col = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) + SCALAR_VAL(2.0) * d  # 1 + 2*d
        alpha_row = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) + SCALAR_VAL(2.0) * a  # 1 + 2*a

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Time stepping loop (must remain sequential).
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):

        #==============================================================
        # Column sweep: for each interior column i, solve in j for v(·, i)
        # Using u(j, i-1:i+1) from time step t as RHS.
        #==============================================================

        # Boundary and initial coefficients along each column (independent in i).
        COL_INIT_BOUNDARIES:
            for i in [1, N-1):
                v[0,     i] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)
                p[i, 0]      = SCALAR_VAL(0.0)
                q[i, 0]      = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)  # = v[0, i]

        # Forward elimination in j (Thomas algorithm).
        # j carries a true dependency; i is fully independent.
        COL_FORWARD:
            for j in seq([1, N-1)):
                for i in [1, N-1):
                    denom_col      = a * p[i, j-1] + b
                    inv_denom_col  = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) / denom_col   # shared between p and q

                    p[i, j] = -c * inv_denom_col

                    q[i, j] =
                        ( -d * u[j, i-1]
                          + alpha_col * u[j, i]
                          - f * u[j, i+1]
                          - a * q[i, j-1]
                        ) * inv_denom_col

        # Top boundary for back substitution.
        COL_BACKWARD_BOUNDARIES:
            for i in [1, N-1):
                v[N-1, i] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)

        # Back substitution in j, logically from j = N-2 down to j = 1.
        # Implemented with helper index jb in increasing order.
        COL_BACKWARD:
            for jb in seq([1, N-1)):         # jb = 1..N-2
                for i in [1, N-1):
                    v[N-1-jb, i] =
                        p[i, N-1-jb] * v[N-jb, i] + q[i, N-1-jb]
                    # physical j index: j = N-1-jb, so this sweeps j = N-2, N-3, ..., 1

        #==============================================================
        # Row sweep: for each interior row i, solve in j for u(i, ·)
        # Using v(i-1:i+1, j) from column sweep as RHS.
        #==============================================================

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "adi.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(u,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
      {
	u[i][j] =  (DATA_TYPE)(i + n-j) / n;
      }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
 
static 
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(u,N,N,n,n)) 

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("u");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf(POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, u[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("u");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
/* Based on a Fortran code fragment from Figure 5 of
 * "Automatic Data and Computation Decomposition on Distributed Memory Parallel Computers"
 * by Peizong Lee and Zvi Meir Kedem, TOPLAS, 2002
 */
static
void kernel_adi[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int tsteps, int n,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(u,N,N,n,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(v,N,N,n,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(p,N,N,n,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(q,N,N,n,n))
{
  int t, i, j;
  DATA_TYPE DX, DY, DT;
  DATA_TYPE B1, B2;
  DATA_TYPE mul1, mul2;
  DATA_TYPE a, b, c, d, e, f;

#pragma scop

  DX = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)/(DATA_TYPE)_PB_N;
  DY = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)/(DATA_TYPE)_PB_N;
  DT = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)/(DATA_TYPE)_PB_TSTEPS;
  B1 = SCALAR_VAL(2.0);
  B2 = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
  mul1 = B1 * DT / (DX * DX);
  mul2 = B2 * DT / (DY * DY);

  a = -mul1 /  SCALAR_VAL(2.0);
  b = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)+mul1;
  c = a;
  d = -mul2 / SCALAR_VAL(2.0);
  e = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)+mul2;
  f = d;

 for (t=1; t<=_PB_TSTEPS; t++) {
    //Column Sweep
    for (i=1; i<_PB_N-1; i++) {
      v[0][i] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
      p[i][0] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      q[i][0] = v[0][i];
      for (j=1; j<_PB_N-1; j++) {
        p[i][j] = -c / (a*p[i][j-1]+b);
        q[i][j] = (-d*u[j][i-1]+(SCALAR_VAL(1.0)+SCALAR_VAL(2.0)*d)*u[j][i] - f*u[j][i+1]-a*q[i][j-1])/(a*p[i][j-1]+b);
      }

      v[_PB_N-1][i] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
      for (j=_PB_N-2; j>=1; j--) {
        v[j][i] = p[i][j] * v[j+1][i] + q[i][j];
      }
    }
    //Row Sweep
    for (i=1; i<_PB_N-1; i++) {
      u[i][0] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
      p[i][0] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      q[i][0] = u[i][0];
      for (j=1; j<_PB_N-1; j++) {
        p[i][j] = -f / (d*p[i][j-1]+e);
        q[i][j] = (-a*v[i-1][j]+(SCALAR_VAL(1.0)+SCALAR_VAL(2.0)*a)*v[i][j] - c*v[i+1][j]-d*q[i][j-1])/(d*p[i][j-1]+e);
      }
      u[i][_PB_N-1] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
      for (j=_PB_N-2; j>=1; j--) {
        u[i][j] = p[i][j] * u[i][j+1] + q[i][j];
      }
    }
  }
#pragma endscop
}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int tsteps = TSTEPS;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(u, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(v, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(p, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(q, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_adi (tsteps, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(v), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(p), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(q));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(u);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(v);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(p);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(q);

  return 0;
}

                    p[i, j] = -c / denom_col
                    q[i, j] = (-d * u[j, i-1]
                               + center_col * u[j, i]
                               - f * u[j, i+1]
                               - a * q[i, j-1]) / denom_col

        # 3) Column boundary condition at j = N-1 for backward substitution.
        COL_BC_BOTTOM:
            for i in [1, N-1):
                v[N-1, i] = 1.0          # bottom boundary for v

        # 4) Backward sweep along j (Thomas back substitution).
        #    Mathematically: v[j, i] = p[i, j] * v[j+1, i] + q[i, j],
        #    for j = N-2, ..., 1.
        COL_BWD:
            for j in seq([1, N-1)):      # scheduled in decreasing j due to deps
                for i in [1, N-1):
                    v[j, i] = p[i, j] * v[j+1, i] + q[i, j]

        # At this point v holds the intermediate solution after the column sweep.

        # === Row sweep (implicit in i, one independent tridiagonal system per i) ===
        # Same structure but now operating on u using v as input.

        # 5) Row boundary conditions and initial values for the forward sweep.
        ROW_BC_LEFT:
            for i in [1, N-1):
                u[i, 0] = 1.0            # left boundary for u
                p[i, 0] = 0.0            # reuse p,q as scratch
                q[i, 0] = 1.0            # q(i, j=0) = u(i,0) = 1

        # 6) Forward sweep along j (Thomas factorization for each row).
        ROW_FWD:
            for j in seq([1, N-1)):      # j = 1..N-2
                for i in [1, N-1):
                    denom_row = d * p[i, j-1] + e
                    p[i, j] = -f / denom_row
                    q[i, j] = (-a * v[i-1, j]
                               + center_row * v[i, j]
                               - c * v[i+1, j]
                               - d * q[i, j-1]) / denom_row

        # 7) Row boundary condition at j = N-1 for backward substitution.
        ROW_BC_RIGHT:
            for i in [1, N-1):
                u[i, N-1] = 1.0          # right boundary for u

        # 8) Backward sweep along j.
        #    Mathematically: u[i, j] = p[i, j] * u[i, j+1] + q[i, j],
        #    for j = N-2, ..., 1.
        ROW_BWD:
            for j in seq([1, N-1)):      # scheduled in decreasing j due to deps
                for i in [1, N-1):
                    u[i, j] = p[i, j] * u[i, j+1] + q[i, j]

dependencies:
    # Dependencies within a fixed time step t.

    # Column forward sweep recurrences along j:
    # p[i, j] and q[i, j] depend on p[i, j-1], q[i, j-1].
    for t in [0, T), i in [1, N-1), j in [2, N-1):
        COL_FWD(t, i, j-1) -> COL_FWD(t, i, j)

    # Column backward sweep recurrences along j:
    # v[j, i] depends on v[j+1, i].
    for t in [0, T), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-2):
        COL_BWD(t, i, j+1) -> COL_BWD(t, i, j)

    # Row forward sweep recurrences along j:
    for t in [0, T), i in [1, N-1), j in [2, N-1):
        ROW_FWD(t, i, j-1) -> ROW_FWD(t, i, j)

    # Row backward sweep recurrences along j:
    for t in [0, T), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-2):
        ROW_BWD(t, i, j+1) -> ROW_BWD(t, i, j)

    # Phase ordering within a time step is given by the nesting/order in 'computation':
    # COL_BC_TOP -> COL_FWD -> COL_BC_BOTTOM -> COL_BWD
    # then ROW_BC_LEFT -> ROW_FWD -> ROW_BC_RIGHT -> ROW_BWD.
    # The outer for t in seq(...) enforces that *all* work at time t
    # finishes before any work at time t+1 starts.

optimization:
    # 1) Tile the i-dimension to improve cache locality and to provide
    #    coarse-grain work units for parallel threads.
    #    IB is a tunable tile size (e.g., 64 or 128, based on L1/L2 sizes).
    block(i, I, IB)

    # 2) Parallelize over the outer i-tiles (dimension I).
    #    Each tridiagonal system along j is independent for each i, so we
    #    can safely run different i-tiles in parallel in both sweeps.
    parallelize(I)

    # 3) Vectorize the innermost i-dimension inside each tile for the
    #    compute-intensive sweeps. The j-dimension remains scalar because
    #    of the Thomas recurrences.
    #    FACTOR can be set to match the SIMD width (e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles).
    vectorize(i, FACTOR)

    # 4) The change of layout for p and q (declared above) is itself an
    #    optimization: it makes p[i, j] and q[i, j] contiguous in memory
    #    when iterating with j outer / i inner, enabling efficient SIMD
    #    loads/stores and reducing cache misses without increasing memory
    #    footprint.

    # 5) Scalar parameters (DX, DY, DT, B1, B2, mul1, mul2, a..f,
    #    center_col, center_row) are already hoisted out of the time loop
    #    in this model; no further hoisting is needed.
--- END OF MODEL: adi-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: adi-03 ---
domain:
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)          # time step index; corresponds to C loop t = 1..TSTEPS
    i: dim in [0, N)               # spatial index in x-direction
    j: dim in [0, N)               # spatial index in y-direction

data:
    # 2D solution arrays, row-major: element (i,j) at linear index i * N + j
    u[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
    v[i, j]: temp  DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Tridiagonal solver coefficients (per line i, along coordinate j)
    p[i, j]: temp  DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
    q[i, j]: temp  DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

parameters:
    # Grid and time sizes
    N:       int       # problem size (both dimensions)
    TSTEPS:  int       # number of time steps

    # Physical / numerical constants
    B1: DATA_TYPE = 2.0
    B2: DATA_TYPE = 1.0

    # Derived scalars (do not depend on t, i, or j)
    DX:  DATA_TYPE = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE) N
    DY:  DATA_TYPE = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE) N
    DT:  DATA_TYPE = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE) TSTEPS

    mul1: DATA_TYPE = B1 * DT / (DX * DX)
    mul2: DATA_TYPE = B2 * DT / (DY * DY)

    a: DATA_TYPE = -mul1 / 2.0
    b: DATA_TYPE =  1.0 + mul1
    c: DATA_TYPE =  a
    d: DATA_TYPE = -mul2 / 2.0
    e: DATA_TYPE =  1.0 + mul2
    f: DATA_TYPE =  d

    # Optional tuning parameters (used only in optimization directives)
    TI: int  # tile size for the i-dimension, 1 <= TI <= N
    VF: int  # vector width (elements) for SIMD along i

computation:
    # Time stepping loop
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):
        #-----------------
        # Column sweep: solve along j for each fixed i, writing v from u
        #-----------------
        for i in [1, N-1):
            COL_TOP_AND_INIT:
                u_top = 1.0           # Dirichlet boundary value
                v[0, i] = u_top
                p[i, 0] = 0.0
                q[i, 0] = v[0, i]     # = 1.0

            COL_FORWARD:
                for j in seq([1, N-1)):
                    # p and q forward recurrence (Thomas algorithm)
                    p[i, j] = -c / (a * p[i, j-1] + b)
                    q[i, j] = (
                        -d * u[j, i-1] +
                        (1.0 + 2.0 * d) * u[j, i] -
                        f * u[j, i+1] -
                        a * q[i, j-1]
                    ) / (a * p[i, j-1] + b)

            COL_BOTTOM:
                v[N-1, i] = u_top    # bottom Dirichlet boundary = 1.0

            COL_BACKWARD:
                # j descends: j = N-2, N-3, ..., 1
                for j in seq([1, N-1)) descending:
                    # backward substitution for v along j
                    v[j, i] = p[i, j] * v[j+1, i] + q[i, j]

        #-----------------
        # Row sweep: solve along j for each fixed i, writing u from v
        #-----------------
        for i in [1, N-1):
            ROW_LEFT_AND_INIT:
                u_left = 1.0          # Dirichlet boundary value
                u[i, 0] = u_left
                p[i, 0] = 0.0
                q[i, 0] = u[i, 0]     # = 1.0

            ROW_FORWARD:
                for j in seq([1, N-1)):
                    # p and q forward recurrence (Thomas algorithm)
                    p[i, j] = -f / (d * p[i, j-1] + e)
                    q[i, j] = (
                        -a * v[i-1, j] +
                        (1.0 + 2.0 * a) * v[i, j] -
                        c * v[i+1, j] -
                        d * q[i, j-1]
                    ) / (d * p[i, j-1] + e)

            ROW_RIGHT:
                u[i, N-1] = u_left    # right Dirichlet boundary = 1.0

            ROW_BACKWARD:
                # j descends: j = N-2, N-3, ..., 1
                for j in seq([1, N-1)) descending:
                    # backward substitution for u along j
                    u[i, j] = p[i, j] * u[i, j+1] + q[i, j]

dependencies:
    # Time stepping: each time step depends on the result of the previous one.
    for t in [0, TSTEPS-1):
        # Entire step t must complete before step t+1 starts.
        ROW_BACKWARD(t, i, j) for all i, j -> COL_TOP_AND_INIT(t+1, i) for all i

    # Within a given time step t:

    # Column sweep per line i:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1):
        # Initialization before forward sweep
        COL_TOP_AND_INIT(t, i) -> COL_FORWARD(t, i, 1)

        # Forward recurrence along j (j increases)
        for j in [2, N-1):
            COL_FORWARD(t, i, j-1) -> COL_FORWARD(t, i, j)

        # Bottom boundary set after forward sweep
        COL_FORWARD(t, i, N-2) -> COL_BOTTOM(t, i)

        # Backward substitution along j (j decreases)
        COL_BOTTOM(t, i) -> COL_BACKWARD(t, i, N-2)
        for j in [1, N-2):
            COL_BACKWARD(t, i, j+1) -> COL_BACKWARD(t, i, j)

    # Row sweep per line i:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1):
        # Row sweep for a given t starts only after the entire column sweep has finished,
        # because it reads v computed in the column sweep.
        for j in [1, N-1):
            COL_BACKWARD(t, k, j) for all k in [1, N-1) -> ROW_LEFT_AND_INIT(t, i)

        ROW_LEFT_AND_INIT(t, i) -> ROW_FORWARD(t, i, 1)

        # Forward recurrence along j (j increases)
        for j in [2, N-1):
            ROW_FORWARD(t, i, j-1) -> ROW_FORWARD(t, i, j)

        # Right boundary set after forward sweep
        ROW_FORWARD(t, i, N-2) -> ROW_RIGHT(t, i)

        # Backward substitution along j (j decreases)
        ROW_RIGHT(t, i) -> ROW_BACKWARD(t, i, N-2)
        for j in [1, N-2):
            ROW_BACKWARD(t, i, j+1) -> ROW_BACKWARD(t, i, j)

optimization:
    #-----------------
    # Scalar and invariant-hoisting optimizations
    #-----------------
    # All coefficients (DX, DY, DT, mul1, mul2, a, b, c, d, e, f) and the
    # Dirichlet boundary value 1.0 are invariant across t, i, j.
    # Hoist their computation outside the t-loop in generated code.
    hoist(t)

    # Within each forward recurrence, the denominator (a * p[i,j-1] + b) or
    # (d * p[i,j-1] + e) is common to the two updates of p and q.
    # A code generator should introduce a loop-private temporary for this
    # denominator to avoid recomputing the multiply-add:
    #   den_c = a * p[i,j-1] + b
    #   p[i,j] = -c / den_c
    #   q[i,j] = (...) / den_c
    # (This reduces work while preserving IEEE-754 semantics, because the
    # multiply-add is evaluated once instead of twice but with identical operands.)

    #-----------------
    # Parallelism across independent 1D lines
    #-----------------
    # For each time step and each sweep, lines indexed by i are independent:
    # the recurrences are only along j. We can therefore parallelize
    # the outer i-dimension.
    parallelize(i) in {
        COL_TOP_AND_INIT, COL_FORWARD, COL_BOTTOM, COL_BACKWARD,
        ROW_LEFT_AND_INIT, ROW_FORWARD, ROW_RIGHT, ROW_BACKWARD
    }

    # To improve cache reuse and load balancing on 32 cores, tile the i-dimension
    # and parallelize over tiles. TI is a tunable tile size (e.g., 32..256).
    block(i, Ii, TI)
    parallelize(Ii)

    #-----------------
    # Instruction-level parallelism and SIMD
    #-----------------
    # j-loops implement a Thomas algorithm and must remain sequential
    # in j to respect the p/q and u/v recurrences. However, within each
    # line i we can expose ILP by modest unrolling of the j loops.
    unroll(j, 4) in {COL_FORWARD, COL_BACKWARD, ROW_FORWARD, ROW_BACKWARD}

    # There are no true dependences along i for fixed (t, j), so within a tile we
    # can vectorize across i. This effectively computes several independent
    # tridiagonal systems in lock-step.
    # A code generator can realize this by strip-mining i inside each tile and
    # mapping the inner i-loop to SIMD lanes.
    vectorize(i, VF) in {
        COL_FORWARD, COL_BACKWARD,
        ROW_FORWARD, ROW_BACKWARD
    }

    #-----------------
    # Memory hierarchy considerations
    #-----------------
    # - Keep u, v, p, q in row-major layout as in the original code.
    # - The i-tiling ensures that each thread repeatedly works on a subset of
    #   rows/columns, improving L1/L2 locality for u, v, p, and q.
    # - No additional large buffers are introduced; extra storage is limited
    #   to a few per-thread scalars (e.g., denominators), well below the
    #   allowed +50% memory overhead.
--- END OF MODEL: adi-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: adi-04 ---
domain:
    # Time dimension
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)

    # 2D spatial grid
    i: dim in [0, N)        # first index in C code
    j: dim in [0, N)        # second index in C code

data:
    # Main solution fields, row-major
    u[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # u[i][j]
    v[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # v[i][j]

    # Tridiagonal solver temporaries, row-major
    p[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # p[i][j], reused each sweep
    q[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # q[i][j], reused each sweep

    # Scalar coefficients (loop-invariant w.r.t. t, i, j)
    DX: scalar DATA_TYPE
    DY: scalar DATA_TYPE
    DT: scalar DATA_TYPE
    B1: scalar DATA_TYPE
    B2: scalar DATA_TYPE
    mul1: scalar DATA_TYPE
    mul2: scalar DATA_TYPE
    a: scalar DATA_TYPE
    b: scalar DATA_TYPE
    c: scalar DATA_TYPE
    d: scalar DATA_TYPE
    e: scalar DATA_TYPE
    f: scalar DATA_TYPE

    # Extra precomputed constants to eliminate repeated arithmetic
    gd: scalar DATA_TYPE      # = 1 + 2*d
    ga: scalar DATA_TYPE      # = 1 + 2*a

parameters:
    N:       int              # spatial grid size
    TSTEPS:  int              # number of time steps

computation:
    # Coefficient setup (once, outside time loop; identical to C code algebraically)
    DX = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE) N
    DY = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE) N
    DT = 1.0 / (DATA_TYPE) TSTEPS

    B1 = 2.0
    B2 = 1.0

    mul1 = B1 * DT / (DX * DX)
    mul2 = B2 * DT / (DY * DY)

    a = -mul1 / 2.0
    b = 1.0 + mul1
    c = a
    d = -mul2 / 2.0
    e = 1.0 + mul2
    f = d

    # Precompute constants that are invariant across all loops
    gd = 1.0 + 2.0 * d       # used in column sweep q-update
    ga = 1.0 + 2.0 * a       # used in row sweep q-update

    # Time stepping: fully sequential in t
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):

        # ============================================================
        # 1) COLUMN SWEEP: solve tridiagonal systems along "columns"
        #    (fix second index i, sweep over j)
        # ============================================================

        # 1a) Initialize boundary conditions and forward-sweep seeds
        #     v(0, i) = 1, p(i, 0) = 0, q(i, 0) = v(0, i) = 1
        for i in [1, N-1):
            v[0, i] = 1.0
            p[i, 0] = 0.0
            q[i, 0] = v[0, i]   # = 1.0

        # 1b) Forward sweep for p and q along j (Thomas algorithm)
        #     Recurrence is along j, i-lines are independent.
        for j in seq([1, N-1)):
            for i in [1, N-1):
                denom1 = a * p[i, j-1] + b        # common subexpression

                p[i, j] = -c / denom1

                q[i, j] =
                    ( -d * u[j, i-1]
                      + gd * u[j, i]
                      - f * u[j, i+1]
                      - a * q[i, j-1] ) / denom1

        # 1c) Set opposite boundary for v
        for i in [1, N-1):
            v[N-1, i] = 1.0

        # 1d) Backward sweep in j to update v using p and q
        #     v(j, i) depends on v(j+1, i), so j must run in descending order.
        for j in seq([1, N-1)) descending:
            for i in [1, N-1):
                v[j, i] = p[i, j] * v[j+1, i] + q[i, j]

        # ============================================================
        # 2) ROW SWEEP: solve tridiagonal systems along "rows"
        #    (fix first index i, sweep over j)
        # ============================================================

        # 2a) Initialize boundary conditions and forward-sweep seeds
        #     u(i, 0) = 1, p(i, 0) = 0, q(i, 0) = u(i, 0) = 1
        for i in [1, N-1):
            u[i, 0] = 1.0
            p[i, 0] = 0.0
            q[i, 0] = u[i, 0]   # = 1.0

        # 2b) Forward sweep for p and q along j using v
        for j in seq([1, N-1)):
            for i in [1, N-1):
                denom2 = d * p[i, j-1] + e        # common subexpression

                p[i, j] = -f / denom2

                q[i, j] =
                    ( -a * v[i-1, j]
                      + ga * v[i, j]
                      - c * v[i+1, j]
                      - d * q[i, j-1] ) / denom2

        # 2c) Set opposite boundary for u
        for i in [1, N-1):
            u[i, N-1] = 1.0

        # 2d) Backward sweep in j to update u using p and q
        for j in seq([1, N-1)) descending:
            for i in [1, N-1):
                u[i, j] = p[i, j] * u[i, j+1] + q[i, j]

dependencies:
    # Time dimension: each time step depends on the previous one
    for t in [0, TSTEPS-1):
        kernel(t) -> kernel(t+1)

    # Within a single time step t, recurrences along j (per (sweep, i)):
    # Column sweep forward:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        (p_fwd(t, i, j-1) -> p_fwd(t, i, j))
        (q_fwd_col(t, i, j-1) -> q_fwd_col(t, i, j))

    # Column sweep backward:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        (v_bwd(t, i, j+1) -> v_bwd(t, i, j))

    # Row sweep forward:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        (p_fwd_row(t, i, j-1) -> p_fwd_row(t, i, j))
        (q_fwd_row(t, i, j-1) -> q_fwd_row(t, i, j))

    # Row sweep backward:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        (u_bwd(t, i, j+1) -> u_bwd(t, i, j))

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Hoist loop-invariant scalar computations
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # DX, DY, DT, B1, B2, mul1, mul2, a, b, c, d, e, f, gd, ga
    # do not depend on t, i, or j. Compute them once before the
    # time loop and treat them as constants during the kernel.
    #
    # This removes repeated divisions and multiplications inside
    # the hotspot loops.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # scalar_hoist: precompute scalar expressions outside loop dim
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    scalar_hoist({DX, DY, DT,
                  B1, B2,
                  mul1, mul2,
                  a, b, c, d, e, f,
                  gd, ga}, t)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Exploit parallelism in the spatial dimension
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # For fixed (t, j), all i-iterations of the forward/backward
    # sweeps are independent (dependencies are only along j).
    #
    # We therefore parallelize across i, using tiling to control
    # cache working-set size and to balance load across cores.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # TI: tunable tile size for i (e.g., 128 or 256 to fit L1/L2)
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    block(i, I, TI)          # tile i into outer tile-dim I and inner dim i
    parallelize(I)           # run tiles in parallel (e.g., via OpenMP)

    # Apply this tiling and parallelization consistently to all
    # i-nested loops in both column and row sweeps:
    #  - Column forward (j outer, I tile, i inner)
    #  - Column backward (j outer, I tile, i inner)
    #  - Row forward (j outer, I tile, i inner)
    #  - Row backward (j outer, I tile, i inner)
    #
    # Boundary-only loops over i (1a, 1c, 2a, 2c) can also be
    # parallelized over I without correctness issues.

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Enable SIMD vectorization along i
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # After restructuring the sweeps to have j sequential and i
    # independent, we can vectorize along i. All accesses in the
    # inner loops are to contiguous memory in the second index:
    #  - u[j, i-1..i+1], v[j±1, i], p[i, j], q[i, j]
    #
    # VW should match the hardware SIMD width for DATA_TYPE
    # (e.g., 4 for AVX2 double, 8 for AVX-512 float).
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    vectorize(i, VW)

    # Optionally unroll the j loops to improve ILP in the presence
    # of recurrences, without changing dependencies:
    unroll(j, 2)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Loop interchange and phase reorganization
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Compared to the original C:
    #  - The forward and backward sweeps were originally nested
    #    as: for i { for j { ... } }, with j as inner loop.
    #  - We have logically reorganized each sweep into four phases:
    #      (init in i), (forward in j), (boundary in i),
    #      (backward in j),
    #    and within the forward/backward phases, we interchange
    #    loops so that j is the sequential outer loop and i is the
    #    inner (vectorizable/parallel) loop.
    #
    # This preserves the j-recursions but exposes much better
    # spatial locality (contiguous access in i) and parallelism.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    interchange(i, j)  # applied to the inner sweeps as described above

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Arithmetic-strength reduction / common-subexpression reuse
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # For each (t, i, j) in the forward sweeps we reuse:
    #  - denom1 = a * p[i, j-1] + b
    #  - denom2 = d * p[i, j-1] + e
    # across p and q updates, avoiding recomputing the denominator.
    #
    # We also precompute:
    #  - gd = 1 + 2*d
    #  - ga = 1 + 2*a
    #
    # so that the inner loops use only multiplications and additions
    # with precomputed scalars, minimizing expensive divisions and
    # repeated additions with constants.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # cse: treat recurring denominators as explicit temporaries
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    cse({a * p[i, j-1] + b,
         d * p[i, j-1] + e},
        scope = {column_forward, row_forward})

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Memory considerations
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # No extra large data structures are introduced beyond the
    # original u, v, p, q. Scalar temporaries and denominators are
    # kept in registers or the stack. The memory footprint therefore
    # stays within the original footprint (well below +50%).
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
--- END OF MODEL: adi-04 ---

--- START OF MODEL: adi-05 ---
domain:
    # Time and spatial dimensions.
    t:  dim in [0, TSTEPS)        # time steps
    i:  dim in [0, N)             # x-direction index
    j:  dim in [0, N)             # y-direction index

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "adi.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(u,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
      {
	u[i][j] =  (DATA_TYPE)(i + n-j) / n;
      }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
 
static 
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(u,N,N,n,n)) 

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("u");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf(POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, u[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("u");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
/* Based on a Fortran code fragment from Figure 5 of
 * "Automatic Data and Computation Decomposition on Distributed Memory Parallel Computers"
 * by Peizong Lee and Zvi Meir Kedem, TOPLAS, 2002
 */
static
void kernel_adi[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int tsteps, int n,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(u,N,N,n,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(v,N,N,n,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(p,N,N,n,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(q,N,N,n,n))
{
  int t, i, j;
  DATA_TYPE DX, DY, DT;
  DATA_TYPE B1, B2;
  DATA_TYPE mul1, mul2;
  DATA_TYPE a, b, c, d, e, f;

#pragma scop

  DX = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)/(DATA_TYPE)_PB_N;
  DY = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)/(DATA_TYPE)_PB_N;
  DT = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)/(DATA_TYPE)_PB_TSTEPS;
  B1 = SCALAR_VAL(2.0);
  B2 = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
  mul1 = B1 * DT / (DX * DX);
  mul2 = B2 * DT / (DY * DY);

  a = -mul1 /  SCALAR_VAL(2.0);
  b = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)+mul1;
  c = a;
  d = -mul2 / SCALAR_VAL(2.0);
  e = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)+mul2;
  f = d;

 for (t=1; t<=_PB_TSTEPS; t++) {
    //Column Sweep
    for (i=1; i<_PB_N-1; i++) {
      v[0][i] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
      p[i][0] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      q[i][0] = v[0][i];
      for (j=1; j<_PB_N-1; j++) {
        p[i][j] = -c / (a*p[i][j-1]+b);
        q[i][j] = (-d*u[j][i-1]+(SCALAR_VAL(1.0)+SCALAR_VAL(2.0)*d)*u[j][i] - f*u[j][i+1]-a*q[i][j-1])/(a*p[i][j-1]+b);
      }

      v[_PB_N-1][i] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
      for (j=_PB_N-2; j>=1; j--) {
        v[j][i] = p[i][j] * v[j+1][i] + q[i][j];
      }
    }
    //Row Sweep
    for (i=1; i<_PB_N-1; i++) {
      u[i][0] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
      p[i][0] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      q[i][0] = u[i][0];
      for (j=1; j<_PB_N-1; j++) {
        p[i][j] = -f / (d*p[i][j-1]+e);
        q[i][j] = (-a*v[i-1][j]+(SCALAR_VAL(1.0)+SCALAR_VAL(2.0)*a)*v[i][j] - c*v[i+1][j]-d*q[i][j-1])/(d*p[i][j-1]+e);
      }
      u[i][_PB_N-1] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
      for (j=_PB_N-2; j>=1; j--) {
        u[i][j] = p[i][j] * u[i][j+1] + q[i][j];
      }
    }
  }
#pragma endscop
}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int tsteps = TSTEPS;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(u, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(v, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(p, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(q, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_adi (tsteps, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(v), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(p), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(q));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(u);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(v);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(p);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(q);

  return 0;
}

    vectorize(i, SIMD_WIDTH)
